requirement:
When `habeas author` assesses a subject with existing evidence, that evidence
MUST only determine whether the subject needs assessment. Its inputs,
determination, and rationale MUST NOT contribute to the mandatory input set
defined by {cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs` or otherwise be
supplied to the model. A new assessment's evidence MUST record only the inputs
supplied to it, so sources that an earlier assessment read but that no longer
exist or are no longer relevant cannot block or shape reassessment.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.ci.authoring_inputs` has no implementation roots, and none is needed. Every clause states observable behavior, not how the code is built. I checked the Implements edges on the requirement and found none.

I looked for a structural obligation in each clause and tried an alternative implementation that keeps the same behavior:

- "that evidence MUST only determine whether the subject needs assessment": this limits what existing evidence affects. Any code layout works, such as a single function or separate modules, as long as the evidence only decides whether to assess. No library, type, signature or named interface is prescribed.
- "Its inputs, determination, and rationale MUST NOT contribute to the mandatory input set ... or otherwise be supplied to the model": this is a prohibition on what reaches the model request. Any code that keeps the old evidence out of the request meets it, however the inputs are built.
- "A new assessment's evidence MUST record only the inputs supplied to it": this describes the content of the output record. Any code that records exactly the supplied inputs meets it.
- The citation of `requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs` only supplies context. That requirement's own text covers how the input set is built.

Because every clause is behavioral, the tests cover its evidence. There is no root that needs an {impl} reference.

behavioral: The obligations and their tests:

1. Existing evidence inputs MUST NOT contribute to the mandatory input set.
   - `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors]` writes old evidence that names `notes.txt`. It asserts that `recorded_inputs()` is empty and that no mandatory input has file `notes.txt`.
   - `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[earlier_evidence_inputs_and_judgments_are_not_carried_forward]` has old inputs that name an existing `notes.txt` and the evidence file itself. It asserts that neither `notes.txt` nor `evidence/` appears in the supplied inputs. The old evidence file is left unchanged.

2. The earlier determination and rationale MUST NOT contribute to the input set or be supplied to the model.
   - Both tests above assert that "old secret judgment" is absent from the serialized mandatory inputs.
   - `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reassessment_records_only_freshly_delivered_inputs]` runs a full `assess` against a recording provider. It asserts that `OLD_RATIONALE`, `deleted.rs` and `fn[old]` are absent from the first prompt sent to the model. It also asserts that they are absent from the new record.

3. The new evidence MUST record only the inputs supplied. Earlier sources that no longer exist or are no longer relevant MUST NOT block or shape reassessment.
   - `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[unresolvable_earlier_inputs_do_not_block_reassessment]` has old evidence naming a missing file, a removed Rust item and a removed requirement. `prepare` still succeeds. The mandatory inputs equal exactly the subject's own declaration.
   - `reassessment_records_only_freshly_delivered_inputs` asserts that the record contains the fresh `requirements.ready` input. It also asserts that no stale strings appear in the record, and that the rationale is the fresh one.

4. The positive clause says existing evidence MUST only determine whether the subject needs assessment. The reviewed tests cover this by checking that evidence has no other effect on the inputs, prompt or record. The staleness and skip decision itself belongs to other requirements, such as the reference-set digest. The bundle test also compares the recorded digest with `reference_set_digest_for`. I found no separate behavioral obligation here that lacks a test.

All four reviewed tests carry `{test}` references to the subject, so there is no marking gap.

The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
